title.zh: 卷五十二 志第二十一: 禮志五
title.raw: 卷五十二 志第二十一: 禮志五 Volume 52 Treatises 22: Rites 5

sentences.zh: 禮志五

translations.literal: Treatise on Rites, Part Five
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Rites, Part Five

sentences.zh: （嘉儀上）〉

translations.literal: (Auspicious Ceremonies, Part One)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Auspicious Ceremonies, Part One)〉

sentences.zh: 皇帝受冊儀：前期一日，尚舍奉御設幄於正殿北墉下，南面設御坐；

translations.literal: Ceremony for the Emperor Receiving the Register: On the day before, Palace Attendants of the Office of Lodging set up a canopy beneath the north wall of the main hall, with the imperial seat facing south;
translations.idiomatic: Ceremony for the Emperor Receiving the Imperial Register: One day beforehand, attendants of the Office of Lodging erect a canopy under the north wall of the main hall and place the imperial seat facing south;

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎設官僚、客使幕次於東西朝堂；

translations.literal: Ceremonial Officers set up curtain pavilions for officials and foreign envoys in the east and west audience halls;
translations.idiomatic: ceremonial officers arrange curtain pavilions for officials and foreign envoys in the eastern and western audience halls;

sentences.zh: 太樂令設宮懸於殿庭，舉麾位在殿第二重西階上，東向；

translations.literal: the Director of the Imperial Music Office sets out the palace bells and chimes in the hall courtyard, with the baton-raising position on the western steps of the hall's second tier, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: the Director of the Imperial Music Office arrays the palace orchestra in the courtyard, with the conductor's station on the western steps of the hall's inner tier, facing east;

sentences.zh: 乘黃令陳車輅；

translations.literal: the Director of the Office of Yellow Horses displays the ritual carriages;
translations.idiomatic: the Director of the Office of Yellow Horses displays the state carriages;

sentences.zh: 尚輦奉御陳輿輦；

translations.literal: Attendants of the Imperial Sedan Chair Office display the sedans and palanquins;
translations.idiomatic: attendants of the Imperial Sedan Chair Office display the imperial litters and palanquins;

sentences.zh: 尚舍奉御設解劍席於東西階。

translations.literal: Palace Attendants of the Office of Lodging set out mats for removing swords on the eastern and western steps.
translations.idiomatic: attendants of the Office of Lodging lay out sword-removal mats on the eastern and western stairways.

sentences.zh: 設文官六品已上位橫街南，東方西向；

translations.literal: Civil officials of the sixth rank and above are assigned positions south of the cross street, the eastern group facing west;
translations.idiomatic: civil officials of the sixth rank and above take their places south of the cross street, the eastern group facing west;

sentences.zh: 武官五品已上位橫街南，西方東向，皆北上重行，每等異位。

translations.literal: military officials of the fifth rank and above are assigned positions south of the cross street, the western group facing east; all advance northward in ranked rows, each grade in a separate position.
translations.idiomatic: military officials of the fifth rank and above stand south of the cross street, the western group facing east; all form northward-facing ranks in rows, each grade in its own station.

sentences.zh: 將士各勒所部六軍仗屯諸門，金吾仗、黃麾仗陳於殿庭。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers each marshal their units of the Six Armies with weapons and station them at the gates; the Jinwu guard detachment and the yellow-banner guard detachment are arrayed in the hall courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers marshal their Six Armies units with arms and post them at the gates; the Jinwu guard and yellow-banner guard detachments are drawn up in the hall courtyard.

sentences.zh: 至日，押冊官引冊自西便門入，置冊案西階上。

translations.literal: On the day itself, the officials escorting the register lead it in through the western side gate and place the register table on the western steps.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day, the officials escorting the register bring it in through the western side gate and set the register table on the western steps.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引侍從班入，就位。

translations.literal: Masters of Ceremonies lead the attendant cohort in and take their places.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Ceremonies lead the attendant cohort in and take their stations.

sentences.zh: 侍中東階下，解劍履，上殿，欄外俯伏跪，奏「中嚴」；

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant, at the foot of the eastern steps, removes sword and shoes, ascends the hall, prostrates himself kneeling outside the railing, and reports, "The inner precinct is secured";
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor, at the foot of the eastern steps, removes his sword and shoes, ascends the hall, kneels prostrate outside the railing, and announces, "The inner precinct is secured";

sentences.zh: 下殿，劍履，復位立。

translations.literal: he descends the hall, resumes sword and shoes, and returns to his standing position.
translations.idiomatic: He descends, dons sword and shoes again, and returns to his post.

sentences.zh: 閣使西階上殿，欄外跪請木契；

translations.literal: The Gate Commissioner ascends the western steps, kneels outside the railing, and requests the wooden tally;
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Commissioner ascends the western steps, kneels outside the railing, and requests the wooden tally;

sentences.zh: 面殿鞠躬，奏「奉敕喚仗。

translations.literal: facing the hall he bows, and reports, "By imperial command, summon the guard.
translations.idiomatic: facing the hall he bows and announces, "By imperial command, summon the guard.

sentences.zh: 」殿中監、少監、殿中丞等押金吾四色仗入，位臣僚後。

translations.literal: " The Directors, Assistant Directors, and Vice Directors of the Palace Service escort in the Jinwu guard's four-colored detachments and take position behind the officials.
translations.idiomatic: " The Directors, Assistant Directors, and Vice Directors of the Palace Service escort the Jinwu guard's four-colored detachments in and take position behind the officials.

sentences.zh: 協律郎入，就舉麾位。

translations.literal: The Music Masters enter and take up the baton-raising position.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Masters enter and take their stations at the conductor's post.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎詣閣奉迎。

translations.literal: Keepers of Seals and Talismans proceed to the inner chamber to escort the emperor forth.
translations.idiomatic: Keepers of the imperial seal and tally proceed to the inner chamber to escort the emperor forth.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引文官四品至六品、武官三品至五品，就門外位。

translations.literal: Masters of Ceremonies lead civil officials of the fourth through sixth ranks and military officials of the third through fifth ranks to their positions outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Ceremonies lead civil officials of the fourth through sixth ranks and military officials of the third through fifth ranks to their stations outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 皇帝御輦至宣德門。

translations.literal: The emperor rides in his palanquin to the Xuande Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rides in his palanquin to the Xuande Gate.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使押內諸司班起居，引皇帝至閣，服袞冕。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat marshals the inner offices in paying respects, leads the emperor to the inner chamber, and he dons dragon robes and ceremonial cap.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat marshals the inner offices in their obeisance, leads the emperor to the inner chamber, and he dons the dragon robes and ceremonial cap.

sentences.zh: 侍中東階下，解劍履，上殿，版奏外辦。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant, at the foot of the eastern steps, removes sword and shoes, ascends the hall, and reports on a tablet that preparations outside are complete.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor, at the foot of the eastern steps, removes sword and shoes, ascends the hall, and reports on a tablet that all preparations outside are complete.

sentences.zh: 太常博士引太常卿，太常卿引帝。

translations.literal: The Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices leads the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and the Minister leads the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices leads the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, who in turn leads the emperor.

sentences.zh: 內諸司出、協律郎舉麾，太樂令令撞黃鐘之鐘，左五鐘皆應，工人鼓，樂作；

translations.literal: the inner offices exit; the Music Master raises the baton; the Director of the Imperial Music Office orders the Yellow Bell bell struck; the five bells to the left all respond; the musicians beat drums, and music begins;
translations.idiomatic: the inner offices withdraw; the Music Master raises his baton; the Director of the Imperial Music Office orders the Yellow Bell struck; the five bells to the left all answer; the musicians drum, and the music begins;

sentences.zh: 皇帝即御坐，宣徽使贊扇合，樂止；

translations.literal: the emperor takes his imperial seat; the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat calls for the fans to close, and the music stops;
translations.idiomatic: the emperor takes the imperial seat; the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat calls for the fans to close, and the music ceases;

sentences.zh: 贊簾捲，扇開。

translations.literal: he calls for the curtains to be raised and the fans opened.
translations.idiomatic: he calls for the curtains to be raised and the fans opened.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎奉寶進，左右金吾報平安。

translations.literal: Keepers of Seals and Talismans present the imperial seal; the Jinwu guards on left and right report that all is secure.
translations.idiomatic: Keepers of the seal and tally present the imperial treasure; the Jinwu guards on left and right announce that all is secure.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引文官三品、武官二品已上入門，樂作；

translations.literal: Masters of Ceremonies lead in civil officials of the third rank and military officials of the second rank and above; music plays;
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Ceremonies lead in civil officials of the third rank and military officials of the second rank and above; music plays;

sentences.zh: 就相向位畢，樂止。

translations.literal: when they have taken their facing positions, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: once they have taken their facing positions, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引侍從班、南班文官三品、武官二品已上合班，北向。

translations.literal: Masters of Ceremonies lead the attendant cohort and the southern cohort of civil officials of the third rank and military officials of the second rank and above to form a combined formation, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Ceremonies lead the attendant cohort and the southern cohort of civil officials of the third rank and military officials of the second rank and above to form a combined formation facing north.

sentences.zh: 東班西上，西班東上，起居，七拜。

translations.literal: The eastern cohort advances from the west, the western cohort from the east; they pay respects with seven bows.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern cohort advances from the west, the western from the east; they perform the obeisance of seven bows.

sentences.zh: 分班，各復位。

translations.literal: They separate into formations and each returns to his position.
translations.idiomatic: They separate into their formations and each returns to his station.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引押冊官押冊自西階下，至丹墀，當殿置香案冊案。

translations.literal: Masters of Ceremonies lead the officials escorting the register down the western steps to the red terrace, where before the hall they set out the incense table and register table.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Ceremonies lead the officials escorting the register down the western steps to the red terrace, where they set out the incense table and register table before the hall.

sentences.zh: 置冊訖，樂作；

translations.literal: When the register is set in place, music plays;
translations.idiomatic: Once the register is set in place, music plays;

sentences.zh: 就位，樂止。

translations.literal: when they have taken their positions, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: once they have taken their stations, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 捧冊官近後，東西相對立。

translations.literal: The officials bearing the register stand close behind, facing each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: The officials bearing the register stand close behind, facing each other on the east and west.

sentences.zh: 舍人引侍從班並南班合班，北向如初。

translations.literal: Masters of Ceremonies lead the attendant cohort and the southern cohort to form a combined formation, facing north as before.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Ceremonies lead the attendant cohort and the southern cohort to form a combined formation facing north as before.

sentences.zh: 贊再拜，在位者皆再拜；

translations.literal: The herald calls for a double bow; all those in position perform a double bow;
translations.idiomatic: The herald calls for a double bow; all those in position bow twice;

sentences.zh: 舞蹈，五拜。

translations.literal: they perform the ceremonial dance and five bows.
translations.idiomatic: they perform the ceremonial dance and five bows.

sentences.zh: 分班，各復位如初。

translations.literal: They separate into formations and each returns to his original position.
translations.idiomatic: They separate into formations and each returns to his original station.

sentences.zh: 捧冊官就西階下解劍席，解劍履，捧冊西階上殿，樂作；

translations.literal: The officials bearing the register go to the sword-removal mat at the foot of the western steps, remove sword and shoes, ascend the hall by the western steps bearing the register; music plays;
translations.idiomatic: The officials bearing the register go to the sword-removal mat at the foot of the western steps, remove sword and shoes, and ascend the hall by the western steps with the register; music plays;

sentences.zh: 置冊御坐前，東西立，北向。

translations.literal: they set the register before the imperial seat, standing east and west, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: they set the register before the imperial seat, standing on the east and west, facing north.

sentences.zh: 捧冊官西墉下立，北上，樂止。

translations.literal: The officials bearing the register stand below the western wall, facing north; the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The officials bearing the register stand below the western wall, facing north; the music stops.

sentences.zh: 讀冊官出班，當殿立，贊再拜，三呼「萬歲」，就西階下解劍席，解劍履，西階上殿，欄內立，當御坐前。

translations.literal: The official reading the register steps forward from the formation, stands before the hall, the herald calls for a double bow, and three shouts of "Long live the Emperor!"; he goes to the sword-removal mat at the foot of the western steps, removes sword and shoes, ascends the hall by the western steps, stands inside the railing before the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: The official appointed to read the register steps forward, stands before the hall, the herald calls for a double bow, and three shouts of "Long live the Emperor!"; he goes to the sword-removal mat at the foot of the western steps, removes sword and shoes, ascends by the western steps, and stands inside the railing before the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 侍中取冊，捧冊官捧冊匣至讀冊官前跪，相對捧冊。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant takes the register; the officials bearing the register bring the register case before the reading official and kneel, both holding the register facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor takes the register; the officials bearing the register bring the register case before the reading official and kneel, both holding the register facing each other.

sentences.zh: 讀冊官俯伏跪；

translations.literal: The reading official prostrates himself kneeling;
translations.idiomatic: The reading official kneels prostrate;

sentences.zh: 讀訖，俯伏興。

translations.literal: when the reading is finished, he prostrates himself and rises.
translations.idiomatic: when the reading is finished, he prostrates himself and rises.

sentences.zh: 捧冊官跪左膝，以冊授侍中。

translations.literal: The official bearing the register kneels on his left knee and hands the register to the Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The official bearing the register kneels on his left knee and hands the register to the Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 侍中受冊，以冊授執事者，降自西階，劍履訖，復當殿位。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant receives the register and hands it to the attendant official; he descends by the western steps, resumes sword and shoes, and returns to his position before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor receives the register and hands it to the attendant official; he descends by the western steps, dons sword and shoes, and returns to his position before the hall.

sentences.zh: 贊再拜，三呼「萬歲」，復分班位。

translations.literal: The herald calls for a double bow and three shouts of "Long live the Emperor!"; they return to their separate formations.
translations.idiomatic: The herald calls for a double bow and three shouts of "Long live the Emperor!"; they return to their separate formations.

sentences.zh: 舍人引侍從班、南班合班，北向如初。

translations.literal: Masters of Ceremonies lead the attendant cohort and southern cohort to form a combined formation, facing north as before.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Ceremonies lead the attendant cohort and southern cohort to form a combined formation facing north as before.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，在位者皆拜；

translations.literal: The herald calls for bows; all those in position bow;
translations.idiomatic: The herald calls for bows; all those in position bow;

sentences.zh: 舞蹈、鞠躬如初。

translations.literal: they perform the ceremonial dance and bow as before.
translations.idiomatic: they perform the ceremonial dance and bow as before.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引班首西階下，解劍履。

translations.literal: Masters of Ceremonies lead the head of the formation to the foot of the western steps to remove sword and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Ceremonies lead the head of the formation to the foot of the western steps to remove sword and shoes.

sentences.zh: 上殿，樂作；

translations.literal: He ascends the hall; music plays;
translations.idiomatic: He ascends the hall; music plays;

sentences.zh: 就欄內位，樂止。

translations.literal: he takes his position inside the railing; the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: he takes his position inside the railing; the music stops.

sentences.zh: 俯伏跪，通全銜臣某等致詞稱賀訖，俯伏興。

translations.literal: He prostrates himself kneeling, delivers a congratulatory address with his full official title, "Your subject So-and-so and others offer congratulations," then prostrates himself and rises.
translations.idiomatic: He kneels prostrate, delivers a congratulatory address with his full official title—"Your subject So-and-so and others offer congratulations"—then prostrates himself and rises.

sentences.zh: 降西階下，帶劍，納舄，樂作；

translations.literal: He descends the western steps, girds on his sword, puts on his shoes; music plays;
translations.idiomatic: He descends the western steps, girds on his sword, puts on his shoes; music plays;

sentences.zh: 復位，樂止。

translations.literal: he returns to his position; the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: he returns to his station; the music stops.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，在位者皆再拜，舞蹈，五拜，鞠躬。

translations.literal: The herald calls for bows; all those in position perform a double bow, the ceremonial dance, five bows, and a bow.
translations.idiomatic: The herald calls for bows; all those in position bow twice, perform the ceremonial dance, five bows, and a bow.

sentences.zh: 侍中臨軒西向，稱「有制」，皆再拜。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant, facing west before the hall, announces, "There is an edict"; all perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor, facing west before the hall, announces, "There is an edict"; all bow twice.

sentences.zh: 侍中宣答訖，贊皆再拜，舞蹈，五拜，分班各復位。

translations.literal: When the Palace Attendant has finished proclaiming the imperial response, the herald calls for all to perform a double bow, the ceremonial dance, and five bows; they separate into formations and each returns to his position.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Counselor has finished proclaiming the imperial response, the herald calls for all to bow twice, perform the ceremonial dance, and five bows; they separate into formations and each returns to his station.

sentences.zh: 三品已上出，樂作；

translations.literal: Those of the third rank and above exit; music plays;
translations.idiomatic: Those of the third rank and above withdraw; music plays;

sentences.zh: 出門畢，樂止。

translations.literal: when all have exited the gate, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: once all have passed through the gate, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 侍中當御坐俯伏跪，通全銜奏「禮畢」，俯伏興。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant, before the imperial seat, prostrates himself kneeling and reports with his full official title, "The ceremony is complete," then prostrates himself and rises.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor, before the imperial seat, kneels prostrate and reports with his full official title, "The ceremony is complete," then prostrates himself and rises.

sentences.zh: 退，東階下殿，帶劍，納履，復位。

translations.literal: He withdraws, descends the hall by the eastern steps, girds on his sword, puts on his shoes, and returns to his position.
translations.idiomatic: He withdraws, descends the hall by the eastern steps, girds on his sword, puts on his shoes, and returns to his post.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使贊扇合，下簾。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat calls for the fans to close and the curtains to be lowered.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat calls for the fans to close and the curtains to be lowered.

sentences.zh: 太常博士、太常卿引皇帝起，樂作；

translations.literal: The Doctor and Minister of Imperial Sacrifices lead the emperor to rise; music plays;
translations.idiomatic: The Doctor and Minister of Imperial Sacrifices lead the emperor to rise; music plays;

sentences.zh: 至閣，樂止。

translations.literal: when he reaches the inner chamber, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: once he reaches the inner chamber, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 舍人引文官四品、武官三品以下出門外，分班立；

translations.literal: Masters of Ceremonies lead civil officials of the fourth rank and military officials of the third rank and below out beyond the gate, where they stand in separate formations;
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Ceremonies lead civil officials of the fourth rank and military officials of the third rank and below out beyond the gate, where they stand in separate formations;

sentences.zh: 次引侍從班出，次兵部、吏部出，次金吾出，次起居郎、舍人出，次殿中監、少監押金吾細仗出，仍位臣僚後。

translations.literal: next they lead the attendant cohort out, next the Ministry of War and Ministry of Personnel, next the Jinwu guard, next the Diarists and Masters of Ceremonies, next the Directors and Assistant Directors of the Palace Service escorting the Jinwu fine guard detachment out, still taking position behind the officials.
translations.idiomatic: next they lead the attendant cohort out, then the Ministry of War and Ministry of Personnel, then the Jinwu guard, then the Diarists and Masters of Ceremonies, then the Directors and Assistant Directors of the Palace Service escorting the Jinwu fine guard detachment out, still taking position behind the officials.

sentences.zh: 次東西上閣門使於丹墀內鞠躬，奏衙內無事，卷班出。

translations.literal: next the eastern and western Gate Commissioners bow within the red terrace and report, "There is no business within the court," and the formation is dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: next the eastern and western Gate Commissioners bow within the red terrace and report, "There is no business within the court," and the formation is dismissed.

sentences.zh: 閣門使丹墀內鞠躬，揖「奉敕放仗」。

translations.literal: The Gate Commissioner bows within the red terrace and announces, "By imperial command, dismiss the guard."
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Commissioner bows within the red terrace and announces, "By imperial command, dismiss the guard."

sentences.zh: 出，門外文武班中間立，喚承受官。

translations.literal: He exits; the civil and military formations stand between them outside the gate, and the receiving official is summoned.
translations.idiomatic: He exits; the civil and military formations stand between them outside the gate, and the receiving official is summoned.

sentences.zh: 承受官聲喏，至閣使後，鞠躬，揖。

translations.literal: The receiving official calls out his acknowledgment, proceeds behind the Gate Commissioner, bows, and announces.
translations.idiomatic: The receiving official calls out his acknowledgment, proceeds behind the Gate Commissioner, bows, and announces.

sentences.zh: 閣使鞠躬，稱「奉敕放仗」。

translations.literal: The Gate Commissioner bows and announces, "By imperial command, dismiss the guard."
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Commissioner bows and announces, "By imperial command, dismiss the guard."

sentences.zh: 承受聲喏，鞠躬，揖，平身立，引聲「奉敕放仗」。

translations.literal: The receiving official calls out his acknowledgment, bows, announces, stands upright, and leads the call, "By imperial command, dismiss the guard."
translations.idiomatic: The receiving official calls out his acknowledgment, bows, announces, stands upright, and leads the call, "By imperial command, dismiss the guard."

sentences.zh: 聲絕，趨退。

translations.literal: When the call ends, he hurries away.
translations.idiomatic: When the call ends, he hurries away.

sentences.zh: 文武合班，再拜。

translations.literal: The civil and military officials form a combined formation and perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military officials form a combined formation and bow twice.

sentences.zh: 舍人一員攝詞令官，殿前鞠躬，揖，稱「奉敕放黃麾仗」，出。

translations.literal: One Master of Ceremonies acts as Commanding Herald; he bows before the hall, announces, and proclaims, "By imperial command, dismiss the yellow-banner guard," and exits.
translations.idiomatic: One Master of Ceremonies acts as Commanding Herald; he bows before the hall, announces, and proclaims, "By imperial command, dismiss the yellow-banner guard," and exits.

sentences.zh: 放金吾仗亦如之。

translations.literal: Dismissing the Jinwu guard is conducted in the same manner.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissing the Jinwu guard follows the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 翼日，文武官僚入問聖躬。

translations.literal: On the following day, civil and military officials enter to inquire after the emperor's health.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day, civil and military officials enter to inquire after the emperor's health.

sentences.zh: 冊皇太后儀；

translations.literal: Ceremony for Investing the Empress Dowager;
translations.idiomatic: Ceremony for Investing the Empress Dowager;

sentences.zh: 前期，陳設於元和殿，如皇帝受冊之儀。

translations.literal: Beforehand, arrangements are set out in the Yuanhe Hall according to the ceremony for the emperor receiving the register.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand, arrangements are set out in the Yuanhe Hall according to the ceremony for the emperor receiving the register.

sentences.zh: 至日，皇帝御弘政殿。

translations.literal: On the day itself, the emperor presides in the Hongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day, the emperor presides in the Hongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 冊入，侍從班入，門外金吾列仗，文武分班。

translations.literal: The register is brought in; the attendant cohort enters; the Jinwu guard is drawn up outside the gate; civil and military officials form separate formations.
translations.idiomatic: The register is brought in; the attendant cohort enters; the Jinwu guard is drawn up outside the gate; civil and military officials form separate formations.

sentences.zh: 侍中解劍，奏「中嚴」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant removes his sword and reports, "The inner precinct is secured."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor removes his sword and announces, "The inner precinct is secured."

sentences.zh: 宣徽使請木契、喚仗皆如之。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat requests the wooden tally and summons the guard—all as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat requests the wooden tally and summons the guard—all as before.

sentences.zh: 樂工入，閣使門外文武班中間立，喚承受官。

translations.literal: Musicians enter; the Gate Commissioner stands between the civil and military formations outside the gate and summons the receiving official.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians enter; the Gate Commissioner stands between the civil and military formations outside the gate and summons the receiving official.

sentences.zh: 聲喏，趨至閣使後立。

translations.literal: The receiving official calls out his acknowledgment and hurries to stand behind the Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The receiving official calls out his acknowledgment and hurries to stand behind the Gate Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 閣使鞠躬，揖，稱「奉敕喚仗」。

translations.literal: The Gate Commissioner bows and announces, "By imperial command, summon the guard."
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Commissioner bows and announces, "By imperial command, summon the guard."

sentences.zh: 承受官鞠躬，聲喏，揖，引聲「奉敕喚仗」。

translations.literal: The receiving official bows, calls out his acknowledgment, announces, and leads the call, "By imperial command, summon the guard."
translations.idiomatic: The receiving official bows, calls out his acknowledgment, announces, and leads the call, "By imperial command, summon the guard."

sentences.zh: 文武合班，再拜。

translations.literal: The civil and military officials form a combined formation and perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military officials form a combined formation and bow twice.

sentences.zh: 殿中監押仗入，文武班入，亦如之。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace Service escorts the guard in; the civil and military formations enter—all as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Palace Service escorts the guard in; the civil and military formations enter—all as before.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使押內諸司供奉官天橋班候。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat marshals the inner offices' attendants in formation at the Tianqiao Bridge to await.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat marshals the inner offices' attendants in formation at the Tianqiao Bridge to await.

sentences.zh: 皇太后禦紫宸殿，乘平頭輦，童子、女童隊樂引。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager proceeds to the Zichen Hall, riding in a flat-topped palanquin, led by boys' and girls' musical processions.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager proceeds to the Zichen Hall in a flat-topped palanquin, led by boys' and girls' musical processions.

sentences.zh: 至金鑾門，閣使奏內諸司起居訖，贊引駕，自下先行至元和殿。

translations.literal: At the Jinluan Gate, the Gate Commissioner reports that the inner offices have finished paying respects; the herald calls to lead the procession, and he descends first to proceed to the Yuanhe Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jinluan Gate, the Gate Commissioner reports that the inner offices have finished their obeisance; the herald calls to lead the procession, and he descends first to proceed to the Yuanhe Hall.

sentences.zh: 皇太后入西北隅閣內更衣。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager enters the inner chamber in the northwest corner to change garments.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager withdraws to the northwest corner chamber to change into ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 侍中解劍，上殿奏外辦。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant removes his sword, ascends the hall, and reports that preparations outside are complete.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor removes his sword, ascends the hall, and reports that all preparations outside are complete.

sentences.zh: 宣徽受版入奏。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat receives the tablet and enters to report.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat receives the tablet and enters to make his report.

sentences.zh: 侍中降，復位。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant descends and returns to his position.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor descends and returns to his post.

sentences.zh: 協律郎舉麾，樂作。

translations.literal: The Music Master raises the baton, and music begins.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Master raises his baton, and the music begins.

sentences.zh: 太樂令、太常卿導引皇太后升坐。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Music Office and the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices lead the Empress Dowager to ascend and take her seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Music Office and the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices lead the Empress Dowager to her seat.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使贊扇合，簾捲，扇開，樂止。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat calls for the fans to close, the curtains to be raised, and the fans opened; the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat calls for the fans to close, the curtains to rise, and the fans to open; the music ceases.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎奉寶置皇太后坐右。

translations.literal: Keepers of Seals and Talismans present the imperial treasure and place it to the right of the Empress Dowager's seat.
translations.idiomatic: Keepers of the seal and tally present the imperial treasure and set it to the right of the Empress Dowager's seat.

sentences.zh: 左右金吾大將軍對揖，鞠躬，奏「軍國內外平安」。

translations.literal: The Jinwu Grand Generals on left and right bow to each other, bow, and report, "Within the army and state, within and without, all is secure."
translations.idiomatic: The Jinwu Grand Generals on left and right bow to each other, bow again, and announce, "Within the army and state, within and without, all is secure."

sentences.zh: 東上閣門副使引丞相東門入，西上閣門副使引親王西門入，通事舍人引文武班入，如儀，樂作；

translations.literal: The Assistant Gate Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate leads the Chancellor in through the eastern gate; the Assistant Gate Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate leads the imperial princes in through the western gate; Masters of Ceremonies lead the civil and military formations in according to ritual; music plays;
translations.idiomatic: The Assistant Gate Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate leads the Chancellor in through the eastern gate; the Assistant Gate Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate leads the imperial princes in through the western gate; Masters of Ceremonies lead the civil and military formations in according to ritual; music plays;

sentences.zh: 至位，樂止。

translations.literal: When they have taken their positions, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: Once they have taken their stations, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 文武班趨進，相向再拜，退復位。

translations.literal: The civil and military formations advance quickly, bow to each other facing one another, withdraw, and return to their positions.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military formations advance quickly, bow to each other face to face, withdraw, and return to their stations.

sentences.zh: 東西上閣門使、宣徽使自弘政殿引皇帝御肩輿至西便門下。

translations.literal: The eastern and western Gate Commissioners and the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat lead the emperor in his shoulder-borne palanquin from the Hongzheng Hall to below the western side gate.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern and western Gate Commissioners and the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat lead the emperor in his shoulder-borne palanquin from the Hongzheng Hall to the western side gate.

sentences.zh: 引入門，樂作；

translations.literal: They lead him through the gate; music plays;
translations.idiomatic: They lead him through the gate; music plays;

sentences.zh: 至殿前位，樂止。

translations.literal: when he reaches his position before the hall, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: once he reaches his position before the hall, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使贊皇帝拜，問皇太后「聖躬萬福」，拜。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat calls for the emperor to bow, inquire of the Empress Dowager, "May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings," and bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat calls for the emperor to bow, inquire of the Empress Dowager, "May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings," and bow again.

sentences.zh: 皇帝御西閣坐，合班起居如儀。

translations.literal: The emperor takes his seat in the western inner chamber; the combined formation pays respects according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor takes his seat in the western inner chamber; the combined formation performs the obeisance according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 北府宰相押冊，中書、樞密令史八人舁冊，東西上閣門使引冊，宣徽使引皇帝送冊，樂作；

translations.literal: The Chancellor of the Northern Administration escorts the register; eight clerks of the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs carry the register; the eastern and western Gate Commissioners lead the register; the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat leads the emperor to present the register; music plays;
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor of the Northern Administration escorts the register; eight clerks of the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs carry it; the eastern and western Gate Commissioners lead the procession; the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat leads the emperor to present the register; music plays;

sentences.zh: 至殿前置冊位，樂止。

translations.literal: when they reach the register position before the hall, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: once they reach the register position before the hall, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使贊皇帝再拜，稱「萬歲」，群臣陪位，揖。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat calls for the emperor to perform a double bow and proclaim, "Long live the Emperor!"; the assembled ministers in attendance bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat calls for the emperor to bow twice and proclaim, "Long live the Emperor!"; the assembled ministers in attendance bow.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士四人、大將軍四人舁冊。

translations.literal: Four Hanlin Academicians and four Grand Generals carry the register.
translations.idiomatic: Four Hanlin Academicians and four Grand Generals carry the register.

sentences.zh: 皇帝捧冊行，三舉武，授冊。

translations.literal: The emperor bears the register as he walks, performs three ritual martial bows, and presents the register.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bears the register as he walks, performs three ritual bows, and presents it.

sentences.zh: 舁之西階上殿，樂作。

translations.literal: They carry it up the hall by the western steps; music plays.
translations.idiomatic: They carry it up the hall by the western steps as music plays.

sentences.zh: 置太后坐前，樂止。

translations.literal: They set it before the Empress Dowager's seat; the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: They set it before the Empress Dowager's seat; the music ceases.

sentences.zh: 皇帝冊西面東立。

translations.literal: The emperor stands west of the register, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stands west of the register, facing east.

sentences.zh: 舍人引丞相當殿再拜，三呼「萬歲」，解劍，西階上殿，樂作；

translations.literal: Masters of Ceremonies lead the Chancellor to perform a double bow before the hall and three shouts of "Long live the Emperor!"; he removes his sword and ascends the hall by the western steps; music plays;
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Ceremonies lead the Chancellor to bow twice before the hall and shout three times, "Long live the Emperor!"; he removes his sword and ascends the hall by the western steps; music plays;

sentences.zh: 至讀冊位，樂止。

translations.literal: when he reaches the reading position, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: once he reaches the reading position, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 俯伏跪讀冊訖，俯伏三呼「萬歲」，復班位。

translations.literal: He prostrates himself kneeling, finishes reading the register, prostrates himself and shouts three times, "Long live the Emperor!", and returns to his formation position.
translations.idiomatic: He kneels prostrate, finishes reading the register, prostrates himself and shouts three times, "Long live the Emperor!", and returns to his formation.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使引皇帝下殿，樂作；

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat leads the emperor down from the hall; music plays;
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat leads the emperor down from the hall; music plays;

sentences.zh: 至殿前位，樂止。

translations.literal: when he reaches his position before the hall, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: once he reaches his position before the hall, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 皇帝拜，舞蹈，拜訖，引皇帝西階上殿。

translations.literal: The emperor bows, performs the ceremonial dance, and when the bowing is finished, they lead the emperor up the hall by the western steps.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bows, performs the ceremonial dance, and when the bowing is finished, they lead him up the hall by the western steps.

sentences.zh: 至皇太后坐前位，俯跪；

translations.literal: when he reaches his position before the Empress Dowager's seat, he kneels prostrate;
translations.idiomatic: once he reaches his position before the Empress Dowager's seat, he kneels prostrate;

sentences.zh: 致詞訖，俯伏興。

translations.literal: when his address is finished, he prostrates himself and rises.
translations.idiomatic: when his address is finished, he prostrates himself and rises.

sentences.zh: 引西階下，至殿前位，拜，舞蹈，拜，鞠躬。

translations.literal: They lead him down the western steps to his position before the hall; he bows, performs the ceremonial dance, bows, and bows.
translations.idiomatic: They lead him down the western steps to his position before the hall; he bows, performs the ceremonial dance, bows again, and bows once more.

sentences.zh: 侍中臨軒，宣太后答稱「有制」，皇帝再拜。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant, facing the hall, proclaims the Empress Dowager's response, "There is an edict"; the emperor performs a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor, facing the hall, proclaims the Empress Dowager's response, "There is an edict"; the emperor bows twice.

sentences.zh: 宣訖，引皇帝上殿，樂作；

translations.literal: When the proclamation is finished, they lead the emperor up the hall; music plays;
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation is finished, they lead the emperor up the hall; music plays;

sentences.zh: 至西閣，樂止。

translations.literal: when he reaches the western inner chamber, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: once he reaches the western inner chamber, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 丞相、親王、侍從文武合班，贊拜，舞蹈，三呼「萬歲」如儀。

translations.literal: The Chancellor, imperial princes, and attendant civil and military officials form a combined formation; the herald calls for bows, the ceremonial dance, and three shouts of "Long live the Emperor!" according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor, imperial princes, and attendant civil and military officials form a combined formation; the herald calls for bows, the ceremonial dance, and three shouts of "Long live the Emperor!" according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 丞相上賀，侍中宣答如儀。

translations.literal: The Chancellor offers congratulations; the Palace Attendant proclaims the response according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor offers congratulations; the Grand Counselor proclaims the response according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 丞相以下出，舉樂；

translations.literal: The Chancellor and those below him exit; music is raised;
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor and those below him withdraw; music begins;

sentences.zh: 出門，樂止。

translations.literal: when they exit the gate, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: once they pass through the gate, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏「禮畢」，宣徽索扇，扇合，下簾。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reports, "The ceremony is complete"; the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat calls for the fans, the fans close, and the curtains are lowered.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor reports, "The ceremony is complete"; the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat calls for the fans, the fans close, and the curtains are lowered.

sentences.zh: 皇太后起，舉樂；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager rises; music is raised;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager rises; music begins;

sentences.zh: 入閣，樂止。

translations.literal: she enters the inner chamber; the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: she withdraws to the inner chamber; the music stops.

sentences.zh: 文武官出門外，分班侍從。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials exit beyond the gate and stand in separate formations as attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials exit beyond the gate and stand in separate formations as attendants.

sentences.zh: 兵部、吏部起居，金吾仗出，如儀。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War and Ministry of Personnel pay respects; the Jinwu guard detachment exits—all according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War and Ministry of Personnel perform their obeisance; the Jinwu guard detachment withdraws—all according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 閣使奏「放仗」，皆如皇帝受冊之儀。

translations.literal: The Gate Commissioner reports, "Dismiss the guard"—all as in the ceremony for the emperor receiving the register.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Commissioner announces, "Dismiss the guard"—all as in the ceremony for the emperor receiving the register.

sentences.zh: 冊皇后儀：至日，北南臣僚、內外命婦詣端拱殿幕次。

translations.literal: Ceremony for Investing the Empress: On the day itself, officials of the Northern and Southern Administrations and court ladies within and without proceed to the curtain pavilions of the Duangong Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremony for Investing the Empress: On the appointed day, officials of the Northern and Southern Administrations and court ladies from within and without the palace proceed to the curtain pavilions of the Duangong Hall.

sentences.zh: 皇后至閣，侍中奏「中嚴」，引命婦班入，就東西相向位立。

translations.literal: When the empress reaches the inner chamber, the Palace Attendant reports, "The inner precinct is secured," and leads the court ladies' formation in to stand in facing positions east and west.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress reaches the inner chamber, the Grand Counselor announces, "The inner precinct is secured," and leads the court ladies' formation in to stand facing each other on the east and west.

sentences.zh: 皇帝臨軒，命使發冊。

translations.literal: The emperor presides before the hall and orders the envoy to issue the register.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor presides before the hall and orders the envoy to issue the register.

sentences.zh: 使副押冊至端拱殿門外幕次。

translations.literal: The envoy and his deputy escort the register to the curtain pavilion outside the Duangong Hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy and his deputy escort the register to the curtain pavilion outside the Duangong Hall gate.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏外辦。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reports that preparations outside are complete.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor reports that all preparations outside are complete.

sentences.zh: 所司承旨索扇，扇上，舉麾，樂作；

translations.literal: The responsible office, upon receiving the imperial command, calls for the fans; the fans are raised, the baton is lifted, and music begins;
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office, upon receiving the imperial command, calls for the fans; the fans are raised, the baton is lifted, and music begins;

sentences.zh: 皇后出閣升坐，扇開，簾卷，偃麾，樂止。

translations.literal: The empress exits the inner chamber and ascends to her seat; the fans open, the curtains are raised, the baton is lowered, and the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The empress exits the inner chamber and ascends to her seat; the fans open, the curtains rise, the baton is lowered, and the music ceases.

sentences.zh: 引命婦合班面殿起居，八拜。

translations.literal: The court ladies are led to form a combined formation facing the hall to pay respects with eight bows.
translations.idiomatic: The court ladies are led to form a combined formation facing the hall and perform the obeisance of eight bows.

sentences.zh: 皇后降坐，樂作；

translations.literal: The empress descends from her seat; music plays;
translations.idiomatic: The empress descends from her seat; music plays;

sentences.zh: 至殿下褥位，樂止。

translations.literal: when she reaches the cushion position below the hall, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: once she reaches the cushion position below the hall, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 引冊入，置皇后褥位前。

translations.literal: The register is led in and placed before the empress's cushion position.
translations.idiomatic: The register is brought in and set before the empress's cushion.

sentences.zh: 侍中傳宣，皇后四拜，命婦陪位皆拜。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant transmits the proclamation; the empress performs four bows, and the court ladies in attendance all bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor transmits the proclamation; the empress bows four times, and the court ladies in attendance all bow.

sentences.zh: 引讀冊官至皇后褥位前，俯伏跪讀訖，皇后四拜，陪位者皆拜。

translations.literal: The official reading the register is led before the empress's cushion position; he prostrates himself kneeling and finishes reading; the empress performs four bows, and all those in attendance bow.
translations.idiomatic: The official appointed to read the register is led before the empress's cushion; he kneels prostrate and finishes reading; the empress bows four times, and all those in attendance bow.

sentences.zh: 引皇后升殿，使臣引冊，置皇后坐前冊案，退，西向侍立。

translations.literal: The empress is led to ascend the hall; the envoy leads the register, sets it on the register table before the empress's seat, withdraws, and stands attending facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The empress is led to ascend the hall; the envoy leads the register, sets it on the register table before the empress's seat, withdraws, and stands attending facing west.

sentences.zh: 命婦當殿稱賀，四拜。

translations.literal: The court ladies offer congratulations before the hall with four bows.
translations.idiomatic: The court ladies offer congratulations before the hall with four bows.

sentences.zh: 引班首東階上殿，致詞訖，東階下殿，復位，四拜。

translations.literal: The head of the formation is led up the hall by the eastern steps; when his address is finished, he descends by the eastern steps, returns to his position, and performs four bows.
translations.idiomatic: The head of the formation is led up the hall by the eastern steps; when his address is finished, he descends by the eastern steps, returns to his station, and bows four times.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏宣答稱「有教旨」，四拜。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reports and proclaims the response, "There is an imperial instruction"; four bows are performed.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor reports and proclaims the response, "There is an imperial instruction"; four bows are performed.

sentences.zh: 宣答訖，四拜。

translations.literal: When the proclamation of the response is finished, four bows are performed.
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation of the response is finished, four bows are performed.

sentences.zh: 班首上殿進酒，皇后賜押冊使副等酒訖，侍中奏「禮畢」。

translations.literal: The head of the formation ascends the hall to present wine; when the empress has bestowed wine upon the envoy, his deputy, and others who escorted the register, the Palace Attendant reports, "The ceremony is complete."
translations.idiomatic: The head of the formation ascends the hall to present wine; when the empress has bestowed wine upon the envoy, his deputy, and others who escorted the register, the Grand Counselor reports, "The ceremony is complete."

sentences.zh: 承旨索扇，樂作，皇后起；

translations.literal: Upon receiving the imperial command, the fans are called for; music plays, and the empress rises;
translations.idiomatic: Upon receiving the imperial command, the fans are called for; music plays, and the empress rises;

sentences.zh: 入閣，樂止。

translations.literal: she enters the inner chamber; the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: she withdraws to the inner chamber; the music stops.

sentences.zh: 分引命婦等東西門出。

translations.literal: They are led separately out through the eastern and western gates.
translations.idiomatic: They are led out separately through the eastern and western gates.

sentences.zh: 冊皇太子儀：前期一日，設幄坐於宣慶殿，設文武官幕次於朝堂，並殿庭板位，太樂令陳宮縣，皆如皇帝受冊儀。

translations.literal: Ceremony for Investing the Crown Prince: One day beforehand, a canopy and seat are set up in the Xuanqing Hall; curtain pavilions for civil and military officials are set up in the audience hall, along with marker positions in the hall courtyard; the Director of the Imperial Music Office arrays the palace orchestra—all as in the ceremony for the emperor receiving the register.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremony for Investing the Crown Prince: One day beforehand, a canopy and seat are erected in the Xuanqing Hall; curtain pavilions for civil and military officials are arranged in the audience hall, along with marker positions in the hall courtyard; the Director of the Imperial Music Office arrays the palace orchestra—all as in the ceremony for the emperor receiving the register.

sentences.zh: 守宮設皇太子次於朝堂北，西向；

translations.literal: The Palace Keeper sets up the crown prince's pavilion north of the audience hall, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: the Palace Keeper sets up the crown prince's pavilion north of the audience hall, facing west;

sentences.zh: 乘黃令陳金輅朝堂門外，西向；

translations.literal: the Director of the Office of Yellow Horses displays the golden carriage outside the audience hall gate, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: the Director of the Office of Yellow Horses displays the golden carriage outside the audience hall gate, facing west;

sentences.zh: 皇太子儀仗、笳簫、鼓吹等陳宣慶門外；

translations.literal: the crown prince's guard of honor, panpipes, flutes, drums, and horns are arrayed outside the Xuanqing Gate;
translations.idiomatic: the crown prince's guard of honor, panpipes, flutes, drums, and horns are drawn up outside the Xuanqing Gate;

sentences.zh: 典儀設皇太子板位於殿橫街南，近東北向；

translations.literal: the Master of Ceremonies sets the crown prince's marker position south of the hall cross street, near the east, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: the Master of Ceremonies sets the crown prince's marker south of the hall cross street, near the east, facing north;

sentences.zh: 設文武官五品以上位於樂縣東西；

translations.literal: positions for civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above are set east and west of the musical ensemble;
translations.idiomatic: positions for civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above are set east and west of the orchestra;

sentences.zh: 余官如常儀。

translations.literal: other officials follow the usual ritual.
translations.idiomatic: other officials follow the usual procedure.

sentences.zh: 至日，門下侍郎奉冊，中書侍郎奉寶綬，各置於案。

translations.literal: On the day itself, the Vice Minister of the Secretariat presents the register, and the Vice Minister of the Central Secretariat presents the seal and cord; each is placed on its table.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day, the Vice Minister of the Secretariat presents the register, and the Vice Minister of the Central Secretariat presents the seal and cord; each is set on its table.

sentences.zh: 令史二人絳服，對舉案立。

translations.literal: Two clerks in crimson robes stand facing each other, each holding a table.
translations.idiomatic: Two clerks in crimson robes stand facing each other, each holding a table.

sentences.zh: 寶案在橫街北西向，冊案在北。

translations.literal: The seal table is north of the cross street, facing west; the register table is to the north.
translations.idiomatic: The seal table stands north of the cross street, facing west; the register table is to the north.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎、中書侍郎並立案後。

translations.literal: The Vice Ministers of the Secretariat and Central Secretariat both stand behind their tables.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Ministers of the Secretariat and Central Secretariat both stand behind their tables.

sentences.zh: 侍中板奏「中嚴」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reports on a tablet, "The inner precinct is secured."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor reports on a tablet, "The inner precinct is secured."

sentences.zh: 皇太子遠遊冠，絳紗袍，秉珪出。

translations.literal: The crown prince, wearing the traveling cap and crimson gauze robe, holding the jade tablet, emerges.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, wearing the traveling cap and crimson gauze robe and holding the jade tablet, emerges.

sentences.zh: 太子舍人引入，就板位北面殿立。

translations.literal: Attendants of the Heir Apparent lead him in; he takes his marker position facing north toward the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants of the Heir Apparent lead him in; he takes his marker facing north toward the hall.

sentences.zh: 東宮官三師以下皆從，立皇太子東南，西向，太子入門，樂作；

translations.literal: Eastern Palace officials from the Three Preceptors downward all follow, standing southeast of the crown prince, facing west; when the crown prince enters the gate, music plays;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Palace officials from the Three Preceptors downward all follow, standing southeast of the crown prince and facing west; when the crown prince enters the gate, music plays;

sentences.zh: 至位，樂止。

translations.literal: when he reaches his position, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: once he reaches his station, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 典儀贊皇太子再拜，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies calls for the crown prince to perform a double bow; all those in position perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies calls for the crown prince to bow twice; all those in position bow twice.

sentences.zh: 中書令立太子東北，西向，門下侍郎引冊案，中書侍郎取冊，進授中書令，退復位。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Central Secretariat stands northeast of the crown prince, facing west; the Vice Minister of the Secretariat leads the register table forward; the Vice Minister of the Central Secretariat takes the register, advances, and presents it to the Minister, then withdraws and returns to his position.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Central Secretariat stands northeast of the crown prince, facing west; the Vice Minister of the Secretariat leads the register table forward; the Vice Minister of the Central Secretariat takes the register, advances, and presents it to the Minister, then withdraws and returns to his post.

sentences.zh: 傳宣官稱「有制」，皇太子再拜。

translations.literal: The Proclaiming Officer announces, "There is an edict"; the crown prince performs a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Proclaiming Officer announces, "There is an edict"; the crown prince bows twice.

sentences.zh: 傳宣訖，再拜。

translations.literal: When the proclamation is finished, he performs a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation is finished, he bows twice.

sentences.zh: 中書令跪讀冊訖，俯伏興。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Central Secretariat kneels, finishes reading the register, prostrates himself, and rises.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Central Secretariat kneels, finishes reading the register, prostrates himself, and rises.

sentences.zh: 皇太子再拜，受冊，退授左庶子。

translations.literal: The crown prince performs a double bow, receives the register, withdraws, and hands it to the Left Assistant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince bows twice, receives the register, withdraws, and hands it to the Left Assistant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎取寶，進授中書令。

translations.literal: The Vice Minister of the Central Secretariat takes the seal, advances, and presents it to the Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Minister of the Central Secretariat takes the seal, advances, and presents it to the Minister.

sentences.zh: 皇太子進受寶，退授左庶子。

translations.literal: The crown prince advances, receives the seal, withdraws, and hands it to the Left Assistant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince advances, receives the seal, withdraws, and hands it to the Left Assistant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 中書令以下退，復位。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Central Secretariat and those below him withdraw and return to their positions.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Central Secretariat and those below him withdraw and return to their posts.

sentences.zh: 舁案者以案退。

translations.literal: Those carrying the tables withdraw with the tables.
translations.idiomatic: Those carrying the tables withdraw with them.

sentences.zh: 典儀贊再拜，皇太子拜，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies calls for a double bow; the crown prince bows, and all those in position perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies calls for a double bow; the crown prince bows, and all those in position bow twice.

sentences.zh: 太子舍人引皇太子退，樂作；

translations.literal: Attendants of the Heir Apparent lead the crown prince to withdraw; music plays;
translations.idiomatic: Attendants of the Heir Apparent lead the crown prince to withdraw; music plays;

sentences.zh: 出門，樂止。

translations.literal: when he exits the gate, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: once he passes through the gate, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏「禮畢」。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reports, "The ceremony is complete."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor reports, "The ceremony is complete."

sentences.zh: 皇太子升金輅，左庶子以下夾侍，儀仗、鼓吹等並列宣慶門外，三師、三少諸宮臣於金輅前後導從，鳴鐃而行，還東宮，宮庭先設仗衛如式，至宮門，鐃止。

translations.literal: The crown prince ascends the golden carriage; the Left Assistant of the Heir Apparent and those below flank him in attendance; the guard of honor, drums, and horns are all drawn up outside the Xuanqing Gate; the Three Preceptors, Three Junior Tutors, and all palace officials of the Eastern Palace lead the procession before and behind the golden carriage; cymbals are sounded as they proceed; they return to the Eastern Palace, where guard detachments have been set up in the courtyard according to ritual; when they reach the palace gate, the cymbals cease.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince ascends the golden carriage; the Left Assistant of the Heir Apparent and those below flank him; the guard of honor, drums, and horns are all drawn up outside the Xuanqing Gate; the Three Preceptors, Three Junior Tutors, and all Eastern Palace officials lead the procession before and behind the golden carriage; cymbals sound as they proceed; they return to the Eastern Palace, where guard detachments have been posted in the courtyard according to ritual; when they reach the palace gate, the cymbals fall silent.

sentences.zh: 皇太子降金輅，舍人引入就位坐，文武宮臣序班稱賀。

translations.literal: The crown prince descends from the golden carriage; attendants lead him in to take his seat; civil and military palace officials form ranks and offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince steps down from the golden carriage; palace attendants lead him in to take his seat, and the civil and military officials of the Eastern Palace form ranks to offer their congratulations.

sentences.zh: 禮畢。

translations.literal: The ceremony is complete.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony is complete.

sentences.zh: 冊王妃公主儀：至日，押冊使副並讀冊等官押冊東便門入，持節前導至殿。

translations.literal: Ceremony for investing imperial consorts and princesses: On the appointed day, the primary and deputy envoys escorting the register, together with officials who will read the register, bring the register in through the eastern side gate, holding credentials to lead the way to the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremony for investing imperial consorts and princesses: On the appointed day, the primary and deputy envoys escorting the register, together with the officials who will read it, enter through the eastern side gate bearing the register, credentials held before them as they proceed to the hall.

sentences.zh: 冊案置橫街北少東。

translations.literal: The register table is placed north of the cross street, slightly east.
translations.idiomatic: The register table is set north of the cross street, a little to the east.

sentences.zh: 引使副等面殿立而鞠躬。

translations.literal: Guides lead the envoy, deputy, and others to stand facing the hall and bow from the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Guides lead the envoy, his deputy, and the others to stand facing the hall and bow.

sentences.zh: 侍中臨軒稱「有制」，皆再拜，鞠躬。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant, before the hall, announces, "There is an edict"; all perform a double bow and bow from the waist.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor, standing before the hall, announces, "There is an edict"; all bow twice and bow again from the waist.

sentences.zh: 宣制訖，舞蹈，五拜，引冊於宣慶門出。

translations.literal: When the edict has been proclaimed, they perform the ceremonial dance and five bows; the register is led out through the Xuanqing Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict has been proclaimed, they perform the ceremonial dance and five bows, and the register is led out through the Xuanqing Gate.

sentences.zh: 使副等押領儀仗、冊案，赴各私第廳前，向闕陳列。

translations.literal: The envoy, deputy, and others escort the guard of honor and register table to the hall before each private residence, where they are arrayed facing the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy, his deputy, and the others escort the guard of honor and register table to the hall before each private residence, where everything is arrayed facing the palace.

sentences.zh: 設傳宣受冊拜褥，冊案置褥左，去冪蓋。

translations.literal: A prostration mat for receiving the register through proclamation is set out; the register table is placed to the left of the mat; the covering is removed.
translations.idiomatic: A prostration mat is laid out for receiving the register by proclamation; the register table is placed to the left of the mat, and the covering is removed.

sentences.zh: 使副案右序立。

translations.literal: The envoy and deputy stand in order to the right of the table.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy and his deputy stand in order to the right of the table.

sentences.zh: 受冊者就位立，傳宣稱「有制」，再拜。

translations.literal: The recipient of the register takes position and stands; the Proclaiming Officer announces, "There is an edict"; he performs a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The recipient of the register takes his place and stands; the herald announces, "There is an edict," and he bows twice.

sentences.zh: 宣制畢，舁冊人舉冊匣於褥前跪捧，引讀冊者與受冊者皆俯伏跪，讀訖，皆俯伏興。

translations.literal: When the proclamation is finished, the bearers of the register raise the register casket before the mat and kneel holding it; the reader of the register and the recipient both prostrate and kneel; when the reading is finished, all rise from prostration.
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation is finished, the bearers of the register raise the register casket before the mat and kneel holding it; the reader and the recipient both prostrate and kneel; when the reading is finished, all rise from prostration.

sentences.zh: 受冊者謝恩，國王五拜，王妃、公主四拜。

translations.literal: The recipient expresses thanks for the grace; a king performs five bows; an imperial consort or princess performs four bows.
translations.idiomatic: The recipient expresses thanks for the imperial grace; a king bows five times, and an imperial consort or princess bows four times.

sentences.zh: 若冊禮同日，先上皇太后冊寶，次臨軒同制，遣使冊皇后、諸王妃主，次冊皇太子。

translations.literal: If investiture ceremonies fall on the same day: first present the Empress Dowager's register and seal; next, with the same edict before the hall, dispatch envoys to invest the empress and all imperial consorts and princesses; lastly invest the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: If several investitures fall on the same day, the Empress Dowager's register and seal are presented first; next, with the same edict proclaimed before the hall, envoys are dispatched to invest the empress and all imperial consorts and princesses; the crown prince is invested last.

sentences.zh: 皇帝納後之儀：擇吉日。

translations.literal: Ceremony for the emperor taking an empress: An auspicious day is chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremony for the emperor taking an empress: an auspicious day is chosen.

sentences.zh: 至日，後族畢集。

translations.literal: On the day, the empress's clan assembles in full.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day, the empress's entire clan assembles.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，後出私舍，坐於堂。

translations.literal: At dawn, the empress emerges from her private quarters and sits in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the empress leaves her private quarters and takes her seat in the hall.

sentences.zh: 皇帝遣使及媒者，以牲酒饔餼至門。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatches envoys and matchmakers bearing sacrificial animals, wine, and wedding provisions to her gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sends envoys and matchmakers bearing sacrificial animals, wine, and wedding provisions to her gate.

sentences.zh: 執事者以告，使及媒者入謁，再拜，平身立。

translations.literal: Attendants report their arrival; the envoys and matchmakers enter to pay respects, perform a double bow, and stand with bodies level.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants announce their arrival; the envoys and matchmakers enter to pay their respects, bow twice, and stand upright.

sentences.zh: 少頃，拜，進酒於皇后次及後之父母、宗族、兄弟。

translations.literal: After a short interval they bow and present wine to the empress's attendants and to the empress's parents, clan, and brothers.
translations.idiomatic: After a short interval they bow and present wine to the empress's attendants, and to her parents, clan, and brothers.

sentences.zh: 酒遍，再拜。

translations.literal: When wine has been offered throughout, they perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: When wine has been offered throughout, they bow twice.

sentences.zh: 納幣，致詞，再拜訖，後族皆坐。

translations.literal: Betrothal gifts are presented and words of address spoken; when the bows are finished, the empress's clan all sit.
translations.idiomatic: Betrothal gifts are presented and the formal address is spoken; when the bows are finished, the empress's clan all take their seats.

sentences.zh: 惕隱夫人四拜，請就車。

translations.literal: The tiyin's wife performs four bows and requests that she enter the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The tiyin's wife bows four times and asks that she enter the carriage.

sentences.zh: 後辭父母、伯叔父母、兄，各四拜；

translations.literal: The empress takes leave of her parents, paternal uncles and aunts, and elder brothers, each bowing four times;
translations.idiomatic: The empress takes leave of her parents, paternal uncles and aunts, and elder brothers, bowing four times to each;

sentences.zh: 宗族長者，皆再拜。

translations.literal: elder members of the clan each receive two bows.
translations.idiomatic: to the senior members of her clan she bows twice each.

sentences.zh: 皇后升車，父母飲後酒，致戒詞，遍及使者、媒者、送者。

translations.literal: The empress ascends the carriage; her parents drink wine to the empress and speak words of admonition, extending the same to envoys, matchmakers, and escorts.
translations.idiomatic: The empress ascends the carriage; her parents drink a parting cup to her and speak words of admonition, extending the same to the envoys, matchmakers, and escorts.

sentences.zh: 發軔，伯叔父母、兄飲後酒如初。

translations.literal: When the carriage sets out, paternal uncles and aunts and elder brothers drink to the empress as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the procession sets out, her paternal uncles and aunts and elder brothers drink their parting cups as before.

sentences.zh: 教坊遮道贊祝，後命賜以物。

translations.literal: Musicians of the Court Entertainment Bureau block the road with songs of blessing; the empress orders gifts bestowed upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians of the Court Entertainment Bureau block the road with songs of blessing, and the empress orders gifts bestowed upon them.

sentences.zh: 後族追拜，進酒，遂行。

translations.literal: The empress's clan pursue with bows and present wine; then the procession proceeds.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's clan follow with bows and present wine; then the procession continues on its way.

sentences.zh: 將至宮門，宰相傳敕，賜皇后酒，遍及送者。

translations.literal: When they are about to reach the palace gate, the chief minister conveys an imperial message and bestows wine upon the empress, extending it to the escorts as well.
translations.idiomatic: As they approach the palace gate, the chief minister conveys an imperial message and bestows wine upon the empress, extending it to the escorts as well.

sentences.zh: 既至，惕隱率皇族奉迎，再拜。

translations.literal: Upon arrival, the tiyin leads the imperial clan in welcome and all perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival, the tiyin leads the imperial clan out to welcome her, and all bow twice.

sentences.zh: 皇后車至便殿東南七十步止，惕隱夫人請降車。

translations.literal: When the empress's carriage reaches seventy paces southeast of the side hall it stops; the tiyin's wife requests that she descend.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress's carriage reaches a point seventy paces southeast of the side hall, it stops; the tiyin's wife asks that she descend.

sentences.zh: 負銀罌，捧縢，履黃道行。

translations.literal: She is borne with a silver pitcher on her back, silk bands in hand, and walks the yellow path.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing a silver pitcher on her back and silk bands in her hands, she walks the yellow path.

sentences.zh: 後一人張羔裘若襲之，前一婦人捧鏡卻行。

translations.literal: One person behind spreads a lamb-fleece garment as if covering her; a woman before holds a mirror and walks backward.
translations.idiomatic: One attendant behind spreads a lamb-fleece garment as if draping it over her; a woman before holds a mirror and walks backward.

sentences.zh: 置鞍於道，後過其上，乃詣神主室三拜，南北向各一拜，酹酒。

translations.literal: A saddle is placed in the road; the empress steps over it, then goes to the spirit tablet chamber and bows three times—once facing south and once facing north—and pours a libation.
translations.idiomatic: A saddle is placed in the road; the empress steps over it, then goes to the spirit tablet chamber and bows three times—once facing south and once facing north—and pours a libation of wine.

sentences.zh: 向謁者一拜。

translations.literal: She bows once to the usher.
translations.idiomatic: She bows once to the usher.

sentences.zh: 起居訖，再拜。

translations.literal: When the inquiry after health is finished, she performs a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the inquiry after her health is finished, she bows twice.

sentences.zh: 次詣舅姑御容拜，奠酒。

translations.literal: Next she goes to bow before the spirit portraits of her parents-in-law and offers wine.
translations.idiomatic: Next she goes to bow before the spirit portraits of her parents-in-law and offers wine.

sentences.zh: 選皇族諸婦宜子孫者，再拜之，授以罌、縢。

translations.literal: She selects women of the imperial clan who are blessed with descendants and bows to them twice; they are entrusted with the pitcher and silk bands.
translations.idiomatic: She selects women of the imperial clan who are blessed with descendants, bows to them twice, and entrusts them with the pitcher and silk bands.

sentences.zh: 又詣諸帝御容拜，奠酒。

translations.literal: She again goes to bow before the spirit portraits of former emperors and offers wine.
translations.idiomatic: She again goes to bow before the spirit portraits of former emperors and offers wine.

sentences.zh: 神賜襲衣、珠玉、珮飾，拜受服之。

translations.literal: The spirits bestow robes, pearls, jades, and ornaments; she bows to receive them and puts them on.
translations.idiomatic: The spirits bestow robes, pearls, jades, and ornaments; she bows to receive them and puts them on.

sentences.zh: 後姊若妹、陪拜者各賜物。

translations.literal: The empress's elder and younger sisters or younger sisters, and those who accompanied her in bowing, each receive gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's elder and younger sisters, and those who accompanied her in bowing, each receive gifts.

sentences.zh: 皇族迎者、後族送者遍賜酒，皆相偶飲訖，後坐別殿，送後者退食於次。

translations.literal: Those who welcomed her from the imperial clan and those who escorted her from the empress's clan are given wine throughout; all drink in paired groups until finished; the empress sits in a separate hall while the escorts withdraw to eat in the side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Those who welcomed her from the imperial clan and those who escorted her from the empress's clan are given wine throughout; all drink in paired groups until finished; the empress sits in a separate hall while the escorts withdraw to dine in the side chambers.

sentences.zh: 媒者傳旨命送後者列於殿北。

translations.literal: The matchmaker conveys an order that those who escorted the empress line up north of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The matchmaker conveys an order that those who escorted the empress line up north of the hall.

sentences.zh: 俟皇帝即御坐，選皇族尊者一人當奧坐，主婚禮。

translations.literal: When the emperor takes his throne, one eminent member of the imperial clan is chosen to occupy the seat of honor and preside over the wedding rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor takes his throne, one eminent member of the imperial clan is chosen to occupy the seat of honor and preside over the wedding rites.

sentences.zh: 命執事者往來致辭於後族，引後族之長率送後者升，當御坐，皆再拜；

translations.literal: Attendants are ordered to go back and forth bearing words to the empress's clan; the head of the empress's clan leads the escorts forward to stand before the imperial seat; all perform a double bow;
translations.idiomatic: Attendants are ordered to go back and forth bearing messages to the empress's clan; the head of the empress's clan leads the escorts forward to stand before the imperial seat; all bow twice;

sentences.zh: 又一拜，少進，附奏送後之詞；

translations.literal: they bow once more, advance slightly, and submit on behalf the words of those who escorted the empress;
translations.idiomatic: they bow once more, advance slightly, and submit on behalf the words of those who escorted the empress;

sentences.zh: 退復位，再拜。

translations.literal: they withdraw and return to their positions and perform a double bow.
translations.idiomatic: they withdraw to their positions and bow twice.

sentences.zh: 後族之長及送後者向當奧者三拜，南北向各一拜，向謁者一拜。

translations.literal: The head of the empress's clan and those who escorted her bow three times before the one occupying the seat of honor—once facing south and once facing north—and bow once to the usher.
translations.idiomatic: The head of the empress's clan and those who escorted her bow three times before the one occupying the seat of honor—once facing south and once facing north—and bow once to the usher.

sentences.zh: 後族之長跪問「聖躬萬福」，再拜；

translations.literal: The head of the empress's clan kneels and inquires, "May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings"; he performs a double bow;
translations.idiomatic: The head of the empress's clan kneels and inquires, "May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings," and bows twice;

sentences.zh: 復奏送後之詞，又再拜。

translations.literal: he again submits the words of those who escorted the empress, and performs a double bow again.
translations.idiomatic: he again submits the words of those who escorted the empress, and bows twice again.

sentences.zh: 當奧者與媒者行酒三周，命送後者再拜，皆坐，終宴。

translations.literal: The one in the seat of honor and the matchmaker circulate wine for three rounds; the escorts are ordered to perform a double bow; all sit, and the banquet concludes.
translations.idiomatic: The one in the seat of honor and the matchmaker circulate wine for three rounds; the escorts are ordered to bow twice; all take their seats, and the banquet concludes.

sentences.zh: 翼日，皇帝晨興，詣先帝御容拜，奠酒訖，復御殿，宴後族及群臣，皇族、後族偶飲如初，百戲、角抵、戲馬較勝以為樂。

translations.literal: On the following day, the emperor rises early in the morning, goes to bow before the spirit portrait of the late emperor and offers wine; when this is finished he returns to the throne hall and feasts the empress's clan and all officials; the imperial clan and empress's clan drink in pairs as before; acrobatics, wrestling, and horse-racing contests supply the amusement.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day the emperor rises early, goes to bow before the spirit portrait of the late emperor and offers wine; when this is finished he returns to the throne hall and feasts the empress's clan and all officials; the imperial clan and empress's clan drink in pairs as before, with acrobatics, wrestling, and horse-racing contests for amusement.
